title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 57 (Punishment for Personation of Shareholder)

content.overview: Section 57 criminalises deceitful personation of an owner of a company security or interest, share warrant or coupon, where the person thereby obtains or attempts to obtain the security/instrument or receives or attempts to receive money due to that owner.
content.glance: Section 57 criminalises deceitful personation of an owner of a company security or interest, share warrant or coupon, where the person thereby obtains or attempts to obtain the security/instrument or receives or attempts to receive money due to that owner.
content.study: If any person deceitfully personates an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of this Act, and thereby obtains or attempts to obtain any such security or interest or any such share warrant or coupon, or receives or attempts to receive any money due to any such owner, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees. Current-law framing: prove deceitful personation of the owner; obtaining or attempting to obtain the security/interest/warrant/coupon or money due; apply the statutory punishment range.

sections.heading: Prohibited conduct
sections.body: Deceitfully personating an owner of a security or interest in a company, or of a share warrant or coupon issued under the Act.

sections.heading: Required object or result
sections.body: By the personation, obtaining or attempting to obtain the security, interest, warrant or coupon, or receiving or attempting to receive money due to the owner.

sections.heading: Punishment
sections.body: Imprisonment for not less than one year and up to three years, and fine of not less than ₹1,00,000 and up to ₹5,00,000.

sections.heading: Distinction from section 38
sections.body: Section 57 concerns personating an existing owner; section 38 concerns fictitious-name applications and related personation in the allotment process.

examples.title: Personation to obtain shares
examples.body: A person pretends to be a registered shareholder and induces the company to issue a duplicate certificate or pay dividend. Section 57 is engaged.

examples.title: Attempt
examples.body: An attempt to obtain money due to a shareholder by deceitful personation is itself punishable under s. 57.

hypotheticals.question: Is attempt enough under s. 57?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The section covers obtaining or attempting to obtain the security/interest/warrant/coupon, and receiving or attempting to receive money due.

distinctions.title: Personation of existing owner and fictitious-name application
distinctions.left: Section 57 concerns deceitfully personating an owner to obtain securities or money due.
distinctions.right: Section 38 concerns personation/fictitious-name conduct in applying for securities.

rows.left: Security, interest, warrant, coupon or money due

misconceptions.trap: Only successful obtaining of shares is punishable.
misconceptions.correction: Section 57 also punishes attempts to obtain securities or money due by personation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is a completed acquisition required under section 57?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. The section covers attempts to obtain the security/instrument or to receive money due to the owner.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How does section 57 differ from section 38?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 57 concerns deceitfully personating an existing owner; section 38 concerns fictitious-name applications and related personation in obtaining securities.
